did_you_know.text: Did you know? At the beginning of the chapter, David gives Solomon his final instructions, guiding him on how to conduct himself as king after David’s death.

Did you know? David uses several different expressions to describe keeping the Lord’s will: walking in His ways and observing His statutes, commandments, ordinances, and testimonies, as written in the Law of Moses.

Did you know? David reminds Solomon of God’s promise to the house of David: if his descendants walk before the Lord faithfully, with all their heart and soul, no one from his line will be cut off from the throne of Israel.
Did you know? David reigned over Israel for forty years: seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
Did you know? After David’s death, Solomon sits on his throne, and the text concludes that his kingdom was firmly established.

Did you know? When Adonijah asks for Abishag the Shunammite, Solomon does not regard it as merely a personal request. He replies that Adonijah might as well have asked for the kingdom, showing that Solomon connects the request with a claim to rule.
Did you know? Solomon removes Abiathar from the priesthood and sends him to Anathoth, and the text notes that this fulfilled the word of the Lord spoken against the house of Eli at Shiloh.

Did you know? Joab flees to the Tent of the Lord and clings to the horns of the altar after hearing of Adonijah’s fate, but Solomon orders him to be executed because he killed Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether.
Did you know? After Joab’s death, Solomon appoints Benaiah son of Jehoiada as commander of the army and Zadok the priest in Abiathar’s place.

Did you know? Solomon allows Shimei to remain alive, but commands him to stay in Jerusalem and warns him that crossing the Kidron Valley will result in his death. Three years later, Shimei goes to Gath to retrieve his slaves, thereby violating the condition.
